intervals.label: array operating
intervals.note: The same paper's abstract says "continuously operating for more than 50 years (since 1970)"; Glushkov et al. (arXiv:0907.0374) say the array "has been observing UHECR events since 1973" and a 2025 Yakutsk paper dates the observation period "1974-2024". 1973 is used where three statements agree.
intervals.quote: it has been continuously operating since 1973

website.quote: The Yakutsk extensive air shower array studies cosmic rays of extremely high energies above 10 PeV

name: Yakutsk Extensive Air Shower Array
notes: The facility and the experiment coincide (the array is the facility); the experiment record is experiment:yakutsk-eas-array.

operator.quote: Yu.G. Shafer Institute of Cosmophysical Research and Aeronomy of SB RAS
operator.value: Yu.G. Shafer Institute of Cosmophysical Research and Aeronomy, Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences

altitude.quote: latitude 61.70 N, longitude 129.40 E, 100 m above sea level (1020 g/cm2)

summary.plain: One of the oldest giant cosmic-ray observatories, in the Lena river valley in Siberia, run by the Shafer Institute in Yakutsk.
summary.technical: Yakutsk EAS array: scintillation, underground-muon and air-Cherenkov detectors on a triangular grid near Oktyomtsy, operating since the 1970s, last modernised 2019-2021, studying cosmic rays above about 1 PeV.
